ledger.claim: Route deviation is not established on this trip's own trace, and the detour ground the platform's support team pressed cannot stand. EV-GPS-00511 measures the driven polyline at 17.41 km against a booked optimal of 17.3 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 0.64% — which fails both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate (excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of optimal), and under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs over the rounded 17.4 km carried on EV-TRIP-00511. The rider therefore carries no detour distance whatever, and a charge defended as a detour charge has no basis in the platform's own data. That matters to the rider because she is the party who has been told, twice, that the driver detoured: on POL-RD-08 the artifacts describe the same trip (TRP-00511 across EV-TRIP-00511, EV-GPS-00511 and EV-FARE-00511, pickup 2026-08-30T07:50-07:56), and nothing in the pool contradicts her account of it.

On the platform's own ledger arithmetic the gap the rider is contesting is SGD 2.3150, not an invention of hers. EV-FARE-00511 computes a recomputed optimal-route fare of SGD 24.0150 against a charged_total of SGD 26.33 — a difference of SGD 2.3150, rounded up to SGD 2.35, which is comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis figure. Under POL-RD-02 the refund is charged_total less the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route, and the ledger has already run exactly that computation. The whole of the difference is elapsed time — 31.0 charged minutes against an optimal 23.0 — and 8 minutes x SGD 0.28 plus 0.1 km x SGD 0.75 accounts for the SGD 2.3150; it is not distance the driver chose. If the judge finds any excess established at all under POL-RD-01, the rider's POL-RD-02 refund cannot be less than SGD 2.35, and the ruling must state charged_total (26.33), recomputed_fare (24.0150) and the refund (2.3150, payable 2.35) on separate lines.

That time component is unexplained on the present record, and the one artifact that could explain it is not in the pool. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the trip; the only advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00511-01, is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0 — so it carries no fact and no exoneration can be run on it. I cite it only for its absence, as POL-GEN-02 permits, and I disclose the impairment: it is weight 0.0 and cannot support an exoneration either way. Under POL-RD-10(5) an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact that is missing from the pool is a mandatory escalation, not a ruling, and the rider asks for exactly that outcome on this limb: the disputed SGD 26.33 held rather than collected, which is what an escalation does under POL-GEN-03.

The rider was billed for a product she did not select, and no clause in this policy reconciles the product booked with the product billed. EV-TRIP-00511 records the booking as taken for RYDE_X with a RYDE_TAXI dispatched, and EV-FARE-00511 bills the trip under rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDETAXI on a METERED fare model with quoted_fare_sgd null — so she had no upfront price protecting her, and the metered time charge, including the eight minutes above the optimal duration, fell on her in full. POL-RD-11's protection is written for UPFRONT_QUOTE trips and is formally unavailable on the fare model the ledger records; POL-RD-02's arithmetic is available only behind a POL-RD-01 deviation that the trace does not establish. That gap between what was booked and what was billed is a matter for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10, and it is the second, independent reason the fee should be held rather than decided by formula.

The rider's account is not to be discounted, and the driver's is not to be credited on assertion alone. EV-RPROF-00511 shows rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the special corroboration requirementPOL-RD-08 imposes on a rider with four or more claims and one or fewer substantiated does not apply to her, and POL-GEN-01 confines those two fields to precisely this test and to nothing else. Against that, the driver's account here is a bare assertion — 'meter fare, standard route' — that points to no artifact and no clause, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight. His only real support is EV-GPS-00511, which shows a route 0.11 km from optimal and therefore supports the rider's version of the trip, not his.

The governing distance figure is the GPS trace. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the trace measures 17.41 km against a booked optimal of 17.3 km, an excess of 0.11 km, which is 0.64% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore fail together: the excess is far below the 0.8 km absolute floor and far below the 20% relative floor. No route deviation is established on this trip.

Because neither POL-RD-01 establishment test passes, POL-RD-01 provides that no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, the only carve-out being a billing-integrity refund which is not in play on this record. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and never restores a charge: this dispute was filed by the rider and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves the metered fare of 26.33 standing and the driver keeps what he was paid.

The rider's own filing concedes the only contested fact in her claim text: 'The DRIVER did nothing wrong, he followed the navigation the whole way.' That concession is corroborated by the trip record, which shows a standard metered run dispatched as RYDE_TAXI, 17.4 km driven on a 17.3 km optimal route with a recorded deviation_pct of 0.6, and by the driver's counterparty statement on file: 'Meter fare, standard route.'

POL-RD-08 puts the initial burden on the rider to show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The trace is unimpaired and measures 0.11 km / 0.64%, so the threshold is not met and the rider's burden is never discharged; no exculpatory clause needs to be reached at all. The rider profile records deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the additional-corroboration proviso in POL-RD-08 is not even engaged.

The driver's device telemetry is admissible and clean: status COMPLETE, weight_multiplier 1.0, 187 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across the whole 31 minute trip, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0. It meets none of the POL-RD-07 impairment limbs (a) to (c), so the excess it reports is dependable, requires no independent corroboration, and there is no data failure that would push this case to escalation.

The ledger reconciles to the cent and contains nothing refundable: base fare 3.80 + 17.4 km at 0.75 (13.05) + 31.0 min at 0.28 (8.68) + 0.80 platform fee = 26.33, exactly the total charged. There are no erp_gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge lines in the breakdown, and the trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom or unmatched charge line to correct as a standalone billing-integrity refund.

POL-RD-06 is engaged only by a MATERIAL deviation, which POL-RD-01 defines as excess above 50% of optimal or above 8.0 km absolute; a 0.11 km excess is nowhere near either limb. Even if the profile were consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither an uplifted remedy under POL-RD-06(b) nor a conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available. This trip stands on its own trace, which is clean.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00511-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. I disclose the impairment: that artifact can carry no fact. Its absence is nonetheless citable, and it is immaterial here, because the driver needs no POL-RD-03 road-closure exoneration when no deviation was ever established against him.

The rider's two grievances - that the app 'kept giving me a taxi' and that the fare exceeded the 22-26 estimate - are not route-deviation grounds. The fare_breakdown records fare_model METERED with surge_multiplier 1.0 read from that artifact, and the trip was dispatched as RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application. On a metered trip the only distance-and-time remedy is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and that clause runs only where a deviation is first established - which on this trace it is not.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties are told the same thing: on this trip's own evidence no route deviation occurred, and the metered fare stands unchanged.

MEASUREMENT (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace governs. EV-GPS-00511 records 17.41 km driven against a booked optimal of 17.3 km on EV-TRIP-00511. The excess is 0.11 km, or 0.64% of optimal. Both establishment gates — greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% — fail, so no deviation is established. On a rider-filed dispute that means NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are, and the driver keeps what he was paid. The rider's own filing and the driver's counterparty statement agree on the driving, and the trace bears them both out.

THE RIDER'S SGD 2.35 CLAIM. The request for the ledger's difference between charged_total 26.33 and recomputed_fare 24.0150 — 2.3150, payable 2.35 — is rejected. POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01, and it is not. The 8 minutes above optimal (31.0 charged against 23.0 optimal) are elapsed time actually incurred on a metered fare, and the rider's own position that the driver followed the navigation is consistent with that. For transparency I state the three figures the clause would carry had it run: charged_total 26.33, recomputed_fare 24.0150, refund 2.3150 (payable 2.35, above the 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share). None of them is payable because no deviation was established.

BILLING INTEGRITY (POL-RD-09(4)). The fare reconciles to the cent: base 3.80 + 17.4 km x 0.75 = 13.05 + 31.0 min x 0.28 = 8.68 + 0.80 platform fee = 26.33. There are no erp_gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no phantom or unmatched charge line to correct, so no standalone billing-integrity refund and no referral under that limb.

ESCALATION IS NOT WARRANTED. The trace is clean: 187 fixes at a 10-second interval, coverage 100%, empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0. It meets none of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment limbs, so POL-RD-10(3) and the escalation route do not fire, and the excess it reports needs no independent corroboration. The rider's call for escalation under POL-RD-10(5) is rejected: that trigger requires an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact missing from the pool, and none is invoked here — there is no deviation to exonerate and no party asserts a road closure, so POL-RD-03 is not in play. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00511-01 (MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) is disclosed as POL-GEN-02(1) requires; it can carry no fact, and its absence is immaterial because the driver needs no closure exoneration. The rider's alternative escalation route (POL-RD-11/POL-RD-10) is also rejected: POL-RD-11 governs UPFRONT_QUOTE fares, and the ledger records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so that clause is formally unavailable rather than unsatisfied.

VOLUME AND PRODUCT. That the booking was taken for RYDE_X and a RYDE_TAXI dispatched is not a route-deviation ground this policy prices, and POL-RD-12 has no application (vehicle_type RYDE_TAXI, no pooled itinerary). POL-RD-06 is not engaged: no material deviation occurred, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither an uplifted remedy nor a driver-conduct referral is available. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is not discharged, so the driver's account need not be tested against it. Both profiles are used only for the tests POL-GEN-01 names, and nothing on either profile carries a finding about this trip.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding fact — the excess measured from the trace against the booked optimal — is carried by EV-GPS-00511 and EV-TRIP-00511, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0; confidence is set at 0.9, comfortably above the 0.70 floor. The one open question — whether the app's substitution of a taxi for the requested cheaper option should have a product-level remedy — belongs in platform review rather than in this ruling, which is why it is noted here and produces no referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
